It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

The Brazilian signed just yesterday but he now has a first Tottenham goal to his name. He cuts inside from the right and drives across the face of the penalty area before firing at the near post, beating Brooks. Tottenham are cruising into the third round and their newest signing scores on his debut.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Tottenham are cruising into the third round and so are Everton, who lead Preston by the same scoreline. Newcastle lead West Brom 3-2 whilst it is still 0-0 between Bradford and Burnley.

Change for Tottenham as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel.

Tel crosses from the left side of the box and picks out Savio, who attempts an audacious flick that does not come off.

West Brom were not back on level terms for long as Barnes has his second of the game and Newcastle lead 3-2 with under 10 minutes remaining.

Charlton have barely threatened the Tottenham goal tonight but that is a decent opportunity for Leaburn, who is played in down the right and forces Kinsky into a decent save.

Savio is straight into the action with good work down the right and squares it for Tel, whose shot is straight at Brooks.

Savio is on for his Tottenham debut and replaces Solanke. Savio only joined Tottenham yesterday but makes his first appearance for the club tonight.

Newcastle had fought from 1-0 down against West Brom to lead 2-1 but Hall has just given away a penalty for the second time in a matter of days having also conceded one in the dying moments of their 2-2 draw against Liverpool on Sunday. Price has stepped up to score his second of the game to bring West Brom level at 2-2 with just over 10 minutes to go.

The Austrian defender has just come on and, with his first touch, puts Tottenham 3-0 up. Fernandes’ free-kick from just outside the box on the right is met by Danso, who attacks it and his header finds the bottom corner. You have to say that goal was coming. Danso has hurt himself as there was a clash of heads as he met the delivery and receives treatment to his head.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

Roberto De Zerbi is turning to his bench and making a triple change as Van de Ven, Danso and Porro come on.

Charlton are also making a triple change of their own.

Gray is found on the left side of the Charlton penalty area and he drives his shot towards goal, forcing Brooks into a decent save. Tottenham are pushing for that third goal.

A cross is sent in from the right and it comes to Tel, who volleys first time but it is a fairly routine save for Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Tottenham are starting to ramp up the pressure as they go in search of a third goal. As it stands, the only side that looks like scoring is Tottenham.

Plenty of cheers from the home fans as Savio is out to warm up. Will Roberto De Zerbi turn to the Brazilian and give him his debut tonight?

One of the new laws brought in this season is to speed up throw-ins and Gray falls foul of taking too long, with Charlton then being given the throw-in.

Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks

Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

“Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”

Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1974. Arsenal receive positive Piero Hincapie injury update ahead of return

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Piero Hincapie has provided some good news for an Arsenal team that have struggled at the start of the season by confirming that he is now fully fit.

The defender has had two separate injury issues since joining Mikel Arteta’s squad but feels he is now over the setbacks and ready to play regularly.

Hincapie is playing for Ecuador in their November international fixtures. His inclusion in the squad was also a positive, as he was unable to play in their last camp due to injury.

Hincapie initially missed Ecuador’s September squad because of a groin problem. He had been named among the substitutes for Arsenal’s final match before that break, against Brighton.

After recovering, the 24-year-old returned to action in the 2-1 Premier League win over Leeds United on October 10. However, he suffered another setback during the warm-down after the match.

The ankle injury was particularly unfortunate, with Hincapie having to leave the pitch with assistance from goalkeeper Illan Meslier. He subsequently missed Arsenal’s matches against Lille and Nottingham Forest.

Mikel Arteta had at first suggested that Hincapie could be out for a matter of weeks, but the defender has since rejoined individual training.

He has now given a much more positive update on his injury whilst on international duty. He is now “100% fit” and does not have any niggles.

This is great news for Arteta. He has had to be cautious with his defensive choices throughout the campaign.

Hincapie will have a chance to get some much-needed game time while he is included in the squad to play Ecuador.

He has been included in the squad by Marcelo Gallardo to face Costa Rica (13th November) and Bolivia (17th November) in friendly games. This will be the first games Ecuador play at home under their new head coach.

Hincapie has also expressed his optimism for his initial discussions with Gallardo. The player is excited to work under the former River Plate manager and help the national team.

He should prove to be a valuable asset in the squad, considering he can play in both roles. He is a natural centre back but can also play as a left back.

Hincapie has shown that he is happy to play anywhere in the team his manager requires. This can be an important factor for Arsenal as the fixture list gets tougher.

He has only featured three times in all competitions this season and has yet to play in the Premier League. Consistent playing time will be key if he is to become a regular in Arteta’s plans.

However, his latest update shows that he is no longer struggling with the physical issues. If he can stay fit over the international break, he will provide another key defensive option for Arsenal in the coming weeks.

#1973. GdS: Tactics, data and team-mates – the ‘strange case’ of Goncalo Ramos at Milan

The Goncalo Ramos enigma continues to dominate the newspaper columns, as AC Milan try unlock their record signing.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport report, Milan fans hoped they had finally found a top-class striker in Ramos, but his three goals this season are not sufficient compared to expectations and the €70m price tag for which he arrived.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

And yet, the Portuguese centre-forward is still proving to be a factor in the team’s fortunes. The reason for this lies behind statistics that the average fan might ignore, but Ruben Amorim certainly isn’t.

The coach has repeatedly emphasised how Ramos is helping the team, less so the other way around. Looking at the numbers, you can’t argue with him. Gonçalo may not be making it into the top scorers’ table, but his work is well explained by statistics that place him among the top strikers in Serie A.

Which ones? Passes (20.7 per game, first in volume among centre-forwards in the league ahead of Lazio’s Noslin) or touches (2nd), for example. But also the aerial duels won and fouls drawn (19, first among attackers) underscore the importance of his sacrifice too.

There are two considerations that don’t emerge from the statistics, but are equally important. The first concerns the movements that free up or facilitate team-mates, such as the sprint for Milan’s first goal in Genoa.

Alphadjo Cisse found himself all alone in the penalty area thanks to Ramos drawing two of the Rossoblu central defenders towards him, allowing Adrien Rabiot to easily pass to the young Italian who was in lots of space.

The second consideration concerns the pressure and coverage work, which has changed since the start of the season. In the early days, Gonçalo was the first to apply pressure up front, but in doing so, he exposed Modric to too much space to cover in front of or behind him.

Amorim therefore asked the Portuguese to instead harass the opposing playmaker, without attacking the defence in the initial possession. This move allows Luka to run less and think more during the opponent’s possession phase.

We were talking about a Milan side that is helping Ramos less than the centre-forward is helping the team, too. The former Benfica man is 19th in Serie A for shots (26) and 15th for shots on target (10).

While it’s true that the Rossoneri maintain a high standard in terms of the quality of chances created (third in the league for big chances behind Inter and Roma), it’s equally undeniable that they arrive in the final third of the pitch less often than expected. Milan are 12th for touches in the opponent’s penalty area and 12th for shots on target.

In short, Ramos sees the ball mostly where he can’t hurt the goalkeepers. Even if, in relation to goal-scoring chances, he should have scored double in the league: 4.16 xG compared to the just two scored. Still, not enough for a Milan-calibre player.

#1972. Arsenal receive mixed verdict after Liverpool penalty review

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

We’ve an important update on the Arsenal Liverpool penalty decision. Arsenal received a mixed reaction from the Premier League’s independent panel after their controversial win at Anfield.

The panel were unanimous in their decision that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty after Jurrien Timber tugged Alexander Isak’s shirt. However, they were divided on whether it should have been reviewed by VAR.

The panel also cleared the officials on the incident involving Noni Madueke. This means that Arsenal were justified in their win due to the wrong decision being made on the penalty.

The incident happened during the 1-0 win for Arsenal at Anfield on November 1. Isak was trying to run onto a cross from Bradley Barcola after Kai Havertz had given the Gunners the lead.

As Timber pulled him back, he was unable to cleanly head the ball. The referee Andy Madley allowed play to continue. The decision was then made by VAR Stuart Attwell that there was not enough evidence to suggest a review.

The five-man Key Match Incidents panel has now ruled that this was the wrong decision. Four of the panel voted that Liverpool should have been awarded the spot kick after Timber’s handball.

However, there was a tight vote on whether VAR should have intervened. Three panellists felt that Attwell should have shown Madley to the pitchside monitor, whilst two felt it did not reach the threshold.

One panellist felt the length of the hold was not long enough to affect the movement of Isak. The other two members who felt that VAR should not have intervened also said that it is subjective as to how much the hold would affect the striker.

This is an important point to note. Whilst they agreed that the penalty was deserved, there was less agreement on whether it was VAR’s responsibility to overturn the decision.

There was also good news for Arsenal in the panel’s decision regarding Madueke’s late altercation with Alexis MacAllister.

The Liverpool midfielder fell to the floor following a headbutt from the Arsenal winger. The incident was reviewed by the VAR, but Madueke was spared a red card. Mac Allister received a yellow.

All five panel members agreed that Madueke should not have been sent off. They felt that there had not been any contact, and Mac Allister’s reaction was certainly excessive.

It certainly gives us an alternative standpoint into the situation. Whilst Arsenal benefited from the incorrect decision regarding the penalty, the officials were backed up with the disciplinary incident.

This won’t have any impact on the result of the Anfield game, as Havertz’s goal was the winning goal and gave Arsenal their first league victory at the stadium in 14 years.

However, it does show how risky Timber was to make the challenge and how close the panel were with whether they should have intervened with VAR.

#1971. West Ham’s Leadership Problem Goes Far Beyond Championship Experience

West Ham’s lack of Championship experience has been highlighted by former striker Sam Parkin, who believes the Hammers are missing the know-how required to negotiate difficult away matches.

Speaking on the Sky Sports EFL Show, Parkin questioned whether West Ham have enough experienced organisers in the team, with The72 highlighting his concerns about a midfield containing Arne Engels, Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa.

Let’s be absolutely clear about this. West Ham lack leaders, full stop. I believe this is partly a consequence of Graham Potter’s clear-out, something highlighted in Michail Antonio’s book, with the former manager appearing to move on some of the bigger personalities at the club. And let’s be fair, they’ve not really been replaced.

However, I think there are two separate issues here. One is leadership, while the other is tactical nous, and I’m not convinced they’re necessarily solved by the same player.

If West Ham are looking for somebody prepared to scrap, they really need look no further than Edson Álvarez. The Mexican is already at the club despite having been frozen out under Nuno Espírito Santo, and he would immediately bring some bite to the midfield.

From a tactical point of view, I suspect Scott Parker will persevere with Soungoutou Magassa in defensive midfield once he gets back up to full fitness. Parker has already brought him back into the picture, and a specialist defensive midfielder could make a significant difference to how West Ham cope when games become physical or untidy.

Longer term, though, there is little doubt West Ham should be looking at the personalities they’re recruiting, not simply the technical ability of individual players.

When Director of Player Recruitment Nils Koppen assesses potential January signings, I’d like to think he’ll be considering whether they can organise those around them, take responsibility and provide leadership when things aren’t going well.

Parkin makes a fair point about Championship experience, but for me the issue goes deeper than knowing the division. West Ham have lost too many big personalities without replacing them, and that’s something Parker and Koppen will eventually have to address.

#1970. Jurgen Klopp faith in Malick Thiaw over Nico Schlotterbeck rewarded with excellent display

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Jurgen Klopp once again putting his trust in the Newcastle United defender.

In his first two internationals in charge, the new Germany boss saw his team concede in both Nations League matches and only pick up one point from a possible six.

Jurgen Klopp then selecting Malick Thiaw in all of the next three and after two clean sheets and four points from a possible six last month for Germany, it was another three points with Thiaw in the starting line up on Friday night.

Germany defeating Serbia 3-1 in Belgrade and the United defender having an excellent game and not at fault for the home side’s consolation goal which came when Germany were already 3-0 up.

There had been eyebrows raised in the German media when Jurgen Klopp selected Malick Thiaw ahead of Nico Schlotterbeck on Friday but that faith in the Newcastle player proving justified.

After the 3-1 win, the Goal player ratings showed only three (midfield/attacking players) with a higher rating than Malick Thiaw’s 7 out of 10, with Goal commenting on Thiaw: ‘Calm and composed at the heart of the defence. Thiaw’s ability to defend in large spaces allowed Germany to push their line high. He recorded several key clearances as Serbia attempted rare counter-attacks.’

Malick Thiaw looked excellent last season for Newcastle United when arriving in summer 2025 from AC Milan but mistakes started creeping in at times during the final months of a tough 58 game season, when too much was probably asked of the defender due to so many injuries.

An up and down start to this season for both player and team overall, saw Matthias Jaissle bring in Schar and Burn for Thiaw and Botman. However, Jaissle brought Malick Thiaw back into the United team at Fulham in the last match and I think paired with Dan Burn this could be the combination to go with for Newcastle this season.

Last night will have been huge confidence boost for Malick Thiaw, his performance against Serbia and the fact Jurgen Klopp kept faith with him for a third start in a row and now only one goal conceded by Germany in their last five hours of football with Thiaw in the team.

Germany are home to the Netherlands on Monday, interesting to see what his selection will be then, last night Malick Thiaw was paired with Jonathan Tah.

#1969. Arsenal face January dilemma as Liverpool and Chelsea join Alex Scott transfer race

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott. Mikel Arteta may have to rethink his transfer plans if competition for the midfielder intensifies.

According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old. The clubs want to establish what it would take to persuade Bournemouth to sell. However, none appears close to agreeing to a deal.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move. Liverpool and Chelsea are more interested in signing Scott in January. However, if they were to make a serious offer, it could be hard to hold out.

Scott has become one of the most exciting midfielders in the Premier League. He is an attractive option for clubs looking to improve their squad going forward due to his age, experience and being a homegrown player.

However, there is some uncertainty around Scott’s future. The England international has turned down two contract offers and is unwilling to sign a new deal. There are 18 months left on Scott’s contract, meaning it is an increasingly important decision for Bournemouth.

Arsenal are interested in Scott with doubts surrounding their own midfield options. There have been reports linking Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino to exits.

Scott would give Arteta another option, but Arsenal will have to consider if they want to make a move and give Liverpool and Chelsea an advantage.

Bournemouth are reported to want more than £100m to let him go during the January transfer window.

It would be a big asking price, especially given that Scott has 18 months left on his contract. There are a few reasons why Bournemouth could be holding out for a big fee.

The Cherries had to pay £25m to bring Scott in from Bristol City, who will receive 20 per cent of any future transfer fee. They will also have to find a suitable replacement at the halfway stage.

Reports said Chelsea received a number of offers worth around £70m in the summer, but Bournemouth have rejected claims that a bid of £80m will get them talking.

Scott is believed to be happy to stay at the club until the end of the campaign. Bournemouth are also having a great season under Marco Rose, currently sitting in seventh place in the Premier League with eight straight wins in all competitions.

Arsenal have little to hurry into any deal and could use the summer to negotiate a better deal. This is especially true with Scott’s contract situation becoming more of an issue.

The problem is that Liverpool and Chelsea are keen competitors and could lead to a bidding war in January, leaving Arsenal with little room to negotiate.

Whilst Arsenal have made their interest known, this doesn’t necessarily mean he will be moving anytime soon. If Scott is a genuine target, then they must be prepared to pounce if the situation arises.

#1968. West Ham Linked With Swansea Star As Magassa Exit Rumours Emerge

West Ham United have been linked with a January move for Swansea City midfielder Marko Stamenić, although I must admit I’m struggling to see why another central midfielder would be a priority for the Hammers.

According to Keith Haynes of Swansea Independent, both West Ham and Southampton are monitoring the 24-year-old New Zealand international. The report suggests Stamenić’s passing ability and defensive awareness have attracted attention, although no formal approach has been confirmed.

West Ham supporters might remember the midfielder from our 1-0 victory over Swansea in October. Stamenić was dispossessed by Divine Mukasa in the build-up to the winning goal, with the young Hammer eventually finishing the move himself. However, that particular incident is hardly a reason to judge a player’s overall ability.

Personally, I think the last thing West Ham need at the moment is another central midfielder. I can think of at least four positions that require strengthening before we start looking to add more players in that department.

We’ve already got Arne Engels, Divine Mukasa, Mohamadou Kanté, Lewis Orford, Tomáš Souček and Soungoutou Magassa, among others. Indeed, the number of midfield options available has been a talking point throughout the season.

More interestingly, the Swansea report also suggests that Magassa could leave West Ham in January, although that remains unconfirmed.

West Ham paid Monaco approximately £20 million for Magassa, but his lack of involvement under Nuno Espírito Santo has hardly helped maintain his transfer value. I would suggest that his valuation has depreciated significantly since arriving at the club.

Given that Scott Parker immediately brought Magassa back into his starting line-up against Cardiff, there is at least some indication that the new manager sees a role for that type of defensive midfielder.

Scott Parker scouted Magassa during his time at Monaco

For me, the sensible approach would be to get Magassa involved in the first team, build up his match fitness and see whether Parker can coax the performances out of him that persuaded West Ham to spend £20 million in the first place.

That would give us a better player and potentially restore some of his transfer value, rather than selling him at what could be a considerable loss.

Stamenić may well be a decent enough footballer, and his reported statistics at Swansea are encouraging. But unless there is a significant departure from West Ham’s midfield, I really don’t see the logic in spending more money on a position where we already have plenty of options.

Surely there are more pressing problems for Nils Koppen to solve in January.

#1967. West Ham Fanzine Blowing Bubbles Shortlisted for National Award

West Ham might be lumbering in mid-table but Hammers fanzine Blowing Bubbles is very much top of class after it was shortlisted for Fanzine of the Year at the 2026 Football Supporters’ Association Awards.

It’s the fourth time the publication has received the recognition, having previously been nominated in 2015, 2021 and 2023. Blowing Bubbles joins five other finalists, including Sunderland’s A Love Supreme, Leeds United’s The Square Ball and Middlesbrough’s Fly Me To The Moon.

Editor David Blackmore launched Blowing Bubbles in the summer of 2012 and has been involved ever since. The publication celebrated its 100th edition in February 2020 and has now reached issue 173, which is quite an achievement for an independent monthly football fanzine.

“I’m absolutely delighted that Blowing Bubbles has been shortlisted for Fanzine of the Year for a fourth time. To be in such an elite group of fantastic football publications is a massive pat on the back and recognition of not only the huge amount of time and effort we put into producing every issue but also to the continued support we’ve had from the West Ham Family.”

Anyone involved in producing independent football content will appreciate the work that goes into keeping a publication going month after month. Credit must also go to David’s team of writers and designer Kelvin Farrell.

The winners will be announced on Monday 30 November at London’s Nobu, Portman Square, with Victoria Derbyshire hosting the FSA Awards. The fanzine category will be decided by a judging panel.

From all of us at Claret & Hugh, congratulations to David and the entire Blowing Bubbles team. Best of luck on awards night. Fingers crossed you bring the trophy home!

#1966. Viktor Gyökeres makes Arsenal future clear as striker responds to exit speculation

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.

The striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season. His latest comments suggest he will not be seeking a move away from north London.

Gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer. He’s played a key role in the club winning the Premier League last season with 14 league goals.

However, he has not featured as much this season. Kai Havertz often being Arteta’s go-to man centrally, resulting in him only starting once in the Premier League.

This has led to some speculation that the Sweden international may look at his options in January. However, his latest interview with the Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen suggests otherwise.

Gyökeres was asked if he wants to stay at Arsenal and has made it clear he wants to continue his career at the Emirates.

The striker also spoke about his relationship with Arteta.

He explained that they regularly discuss football, the team’s approach and the opposition. Those conversations also help him understand what Arteta expects when he is selected to start.

It is a key point to note that just because he hasn’t had much time on the pitch doesn’t mean there have been any issues between the two.

Gyökeres has begun to show his worth again in recent weeks. He found the net against Fleetwood in the League Cup and then Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

This came after a long time to get his first goal of the season and gives him the chance to remind Arteta what he can bring to the team.

There is no doubt that Gyökeres has not lived up to the expectations he had when he came from Portugal.

But his overall effect cannot be ignored. He has contributed 23 goals and 6 assists in 69 games for Arsenal.

The challenge will be finding a way to get the best out of him and Havertz. They add different attributes, and Arteta will have plenty of options to choose from depending on the opposition.

They will also want to avoid losing someone they have invested heavily in so early on. Gyökeres has a contract until 2030, so they are in a great position.

His latest comments will help to reassure fans that he is not looking to leave the club after stating his ambition to play more games and make himself an indispensable part of Arteta’s squad.

The main thing for Arsenal will be to make sure that he can turn this attitude into consistent performances. Gyökeres has made his intentions clear and now needs to show why they brought him to North London in the first place.

#1964. West Ham’s £5m Winger Has Gone From Match-Winner To Liability

Whilst most concentrated on Mads Hermansen’s inability to make saves during West Ham’s 2-1 defeat to Blackburn Rovers, it allowed somebody else to escape the glare of criticism. That player was Manor Solomon, because, to put it frankly, he was awful when coming on as a substitute to replace Edvin Austbø at Ewood Park.

The Israeli international has been shocking for West Ham recently, ironically since the last round of international fixtures in September and October, when he represented his country four times and returned to East London looking completely knackered. His performances have deteriorated to the point where I struggle to see what he’s currently offering the team.

We now find ourselves in the rather strange situation where, with West Ham entering another international break, we’re hoping Solomon can go away with Israel and somehow regain some form. Because as things stand, he is simply not a viable option in the current West Ham team.

No doubt West Ham manager Scott Parker, being something of a Championship expert, would have had reasonably positive opinions of Solomon, having witnessed him tearing up the division for Leeds United during their promotion season. However, he’ll have been left in no illusion that the version of Solomon he’s inherited since replacing Nuno Espírito Santo is a long way from that player.

Solomon stunk the place out in the first half against Cardiff City before being substituted, and when introduced in place of Austbø against Blackburn, he made the team noticeably worse. It’s particularly frustrating because Austbø had looked lively and dangerous, offering the directness and attacking intent that Solomon currently seems unable to provide.

Nuno Espírito Santo pushed hard for the signing of Manor Solomon

It’s important to remember that, whilst West Ham haven’t spent a fortune bringing him in, Solomon was signed for a reported £5 million precisely because he was supposed to guarantee goals and assists in a Championship team. Unfortunately, that looks a long way off at present, and the attacking contribution we expected simply hasn’t materialised consistently enough.

Solomon has been called up by Israel for two UEFA Nations League fixtures during the November international break. He will face Kosovo away on Saturday 14 November before Israel take on Austria in Debrecen, Hungary, on Tuesday 17 November.

The winger also featured in all four of Israel’s September and October Nations League matches, so another spell of international football is hardly guaranteed to leave him refreshed. Nevertheless, West Ham and Scott Parker will be hoping those two games can kick-start Solomon into something approaching his previous form.

There is clearly a talented Championship player in there, as he demonstrated during his time at Leeds. But the player who was supposed to provide West Ham with goals, assists and attacking quality is currently struggling to make any meaningful impact.

Parker has the international break to work with much of his squad, but Solomon will be away with Israel rather than spending that time on the training pitch with his new manager. Perhaps a change of environment and a couple of international appearances will do him some good, because West Ham desperately need the Manor Solomon who helped Leeds win promotion, not the one we’ve been watching recently.

#1963. Jussi Jääskeläinen praises Arsenal star David Raya

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Former Premier League goalkeeper Jussi Jääskeläinen thinks David Raya is the best goalkeeper in the division right now.

But the former Bolton Wanderers star feels the Arsenal No.1 has more to prove before he can be put up with the all-time greats of the competition.

Jääskeläinen recently spoke to Kasinopartio.com, where he praised Raya’s performances and the understanding he has developed with Arsenal’s defenders.

“Raya has been a fantastic signing. He has a great relationship with the centre-backs; even when the back four changes, everything works well.”

The Spaniard has played a key role for Mikel Arteta since his arrival from Brentford. His organisation of the backline, key saves and contribution to Arsenal’s build up play have helped him to be a standout player.

In 2012, Raya began his journey in English football when he moved to Blackburn Rovers from Spain. At that time, he was just a young teenager unfamiliar with English football.

His short spell at Southport introduced him to senior football. Soon, he returned to Blackburn and forged a career ahead of moving to Brentford in 2019. After four years with Brentford, Raya achieved success at the club, helping them to the Premier League.

The player’s performances in the higher leagues caught the attention of Arsenal, and Arteta signed him on loan to the Emirates in 2023 before making the move permanent the following summer.

It didn’t take long for Raya to establish himself in the team. He took home the Premier League Golden Glove, having achieved 16 clean sheets in 32 appearances.

This was a significant milestone in his first season with the Arsenal team, and he has since remained as number one, playing a key role in the club’s pursuit of titles.

While Jääskeläinen said Raya is the best goalkeeper in the Premier League at the moment, he does not think he should be up there with the most experienced.

He believes other goalkeepers have earned an advantage through their consistency over a longer period.

“You have lots of top goalkeepers that I think are still a little bit ahead because of the years they’ve done it in the Premier League.”

“He’s not up there with them yet, but he’s definitely going in the right direction.”

Raya has already proven he can play to the top standard. However, it will be his consistency moving forward that will define his long-term reputation.

Petr Čech, Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar have all gained great reputations over the years. There is still plenty of time for Raya to do the same, but he will need to keep up his high standards whilst wearing an Arsenal shirt.

At just 31, Raya has a lot left in his career. If he can continue playing at this level, it will make the debate around whether he is one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League even more intriguing.

#1962. Repubblica: Milan and Real Madrid watching as Napoli star McTominay stalls on contract

Scott McTominay’s Napoli future is in doubt, and a report has named AC Milan among the surprise potential suitors.

In a Napoli side that appears to have lost its way, one of the few lights leading the way remains McTominay. Despite a season that started on the wrong foot and a heart condition (now resolved), the Scot has five goals in 11 games this season across Serie A and the Champions League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Massimiliano Allegri’s team is going through a tough time, and the former Manchester United player himself has had some tough nights. As La Repubblica (via Calciomercato.com) report, Napoli fans are beginning to worry about where things are heading.

The 29-year-old McTominay is at a turning point in his career, one which has been revitalised since his arrival at Napoli and the Scudetto won under Antonio Conte. His current contract with the Neapolitans expires in 2028, but negotiations for a renewal have stalled.

Fabrizio Romano reported that Napoli remain confident in the possibility of reaching an agreement over an extension, but the uncertainty currently surrounding the project, the bad results and doubts about the club’s future are forcing him to evaluate.

La Repubblica add that the discussions have even stalled after positive steps were taken in September. McTominay and his representatives want to better understand the Azzurri’s vision moving forward before finalising a new agreement.

Sky Switzerland journalist Sacho Tavolieri reported that the former Manchester United man’s agent has already held discussions with several English clubs. Napoli have not completely ruled out a possible sale, and the figure would be €25-30m.

His contract is currently worth €4.5m net per season. Napoli would like to extend it until 2030 with a salary increase, but they are unwilling to accept the Scotsman’s demands, who has requested around €7-8m net per season.

According to La Repubblica, at the end of the season McTominay and Napoli will sit down to discuss the terms of the new contract, once the club’s plans are clearer. Several clubs are interested though and are watching closely.

Aston Villa and Manchester United enquired in the summer. In the coming weeks, Real Madrid and AC Milan will also be keeping a close eye on the developments surrounding McTominay.

Sean Steur was called up in the last international break for the Netherlands Under 21s, a very first time, thanks to his impressive early season Newcastle United form.

The 18-year-old then made his first ever appearance at that level for his country as the Netherlands played out a goalless draw at home to Norway on Friday 2 October, the teenager coming off the bench in the 83rd minute. Ironically it was Kees Smit he replaced, the AZ Alkmaar midfielder who United had been regularly linked with in the past.

A week later and Sean Steur started his first Netherlands Under 21s match, playing the full match and impressing as the Dutch U21s beat their Slovenia counterparts 4-2.

The Newcastle United teenager once again starting for the Netherlands Under 21s on Friday as they faced a crucial match.

In the absence of an injured Kees Smit, extra responsibility on Sean Steur in the first leg of this two-legged European Championship qualifying play-off against the Denmark Under 21s.

The 18-year-old not disappointing as he helped the young Dutch side to a commanding 3-0 win, playing the opening 78 minutes and as well as an outstanding all action display, also providing an assist for the third goal.

The Netherlands U21s now have one foot in the European Championships after this 3-0 win in Denmark, the return leg on Tuesday now looking all but a formality as they look to qualify for the finals of the tournament that will be held next year.

Also on Friday, it ended France U21s 1 Italy U21s 2. Newcastle’s Aladji Bamba playing the final 11 minutes of this friendly, France have already qualified for the 2027 European Championship finals.

#1960. West Ham Youngsters Send Parker Message With Juventus Victory

West Ham United’s Under-21s produced an impressive performance to beat Juventus Next Gen 3-1 at Victoria Road last night, with three different players getting on the scoresheet in the Premier League International Cup.

Harry Montague, Tyrone Omotoye and Jethro Medine scored for the Hammers, who recovered from conceding an equaliser just before half-time to claim their second victory in three matches in the competition. The result moves Mark Robson’s side up to third in Group A with six points.

However, perhaps the most interesting aspect of the evening came from Robson’s comments afterwards. With Scott Parker now in charge of the West Ham first team, the academy coach made it clear that he hoped some of his youngsters had caught the attention of the senior coaching staff.

According to the official West Ham match report, the Hammers dominated much of the opening half and took the lead in the 29th minute.

Preston Fearon delivered a dangerous free-kick into the penalty area, where Montague was on hand to finish from close range.

Juventus equalised through Marco Tiozzo in the 43rd minute, but West Ham continued to create opportunities after the break.

Omotoye restored the lead in the 58th minute, finishing clinically from Jephthah Medine’s cross, before Jethro Medine converted a stoppage-time penalty to complete a thoroughly deserved victory.

Robson was particularly pleased with the contribution of several younger players who had stepped up from the Under-18s.

Speaking to the club’s official website, Robson said:

“We were miles better on the ball than we have been in recent games. I was really pleased with the performance.”

The former West Ham midfielder also highlighted the increased energy and aggression his side displayed compared with their previous defeat against Monaco.

However, it was his final observation that stood out.

“Hopefully, one or two of the lads impressed the first team staff that might have been here this evening.”

It’s an interesting comment given the recent managerial change at West Ham.

As Claret & Hugh recently reported, Robson returned to his Under-21 coaching role during the summer after previously working with the senior squad.

That experience should put him in a good position to judge which youngsters might eventually be capable of making the step up.

There have already been encouraging signs from young players in the first team this season, and Parker will undoubtedly be keen to assess the talent available throughout the club.

Of course, performing well against Juventus Next Gen is very different from playing Championship football. Nevertheless, the academy continues to provide reasons for optimism.

The result also follows another impressive European performance against Valencia earlier in the competition.

West Ham’s next International Cup fixture is against Jong Genk in December, while Robson’s side return to domestic cup action against Brighton Under-21s on 23 November.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. #1959. Mikel Merino speaks out on Arsenal role as January rumours grow

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Merino has played down any speculation around his potential exit during January. He has made it clear he will fight to keep his place in the squad.

He also spoke about speculation around Martin Zubimendi, who has been linked with Atletico Madrid.

Both players have been questioned over their role in Mikel Arteta’s midfield. There is increasing competition for positions at the Emirates.

Merino feels that there is always an intense fight for places in top-level football. He spoke about how strong and deep Arsenal are ahead of their Nations League clash against the Czech Republic.

Both Merino and Zubimendi were also keen to stress that they will be looking to gain more opportunities and not get distracted.

Merino has had to adapt to his new role at Arsenal after playing a key role on his team’s side. However, Merino has struggled to get into the starting XI.

He admitted that he wants to play more games. However, he acknowledged that it was difficult to get into the team, as there are so many quality players.

This shows that his playing time has not affected his relationship with Arteta.

Merino was able to understand what it is like to be a manager because his father was a football coach. He understands that tough decisions have to be made when selecting your starting XI.

This can be an important aspect in a difficult season, as all players need to play their part to make sure Arsenal stay challenging in multiple competitions.

Merino’s comments are very interesting considering the uncertainty around Zubimendi.

There are reports Zubimendi has been linked to Atletico Madrid and whether he will be looking to move in January.

Merino didn’t give a definite answer that these players will stay at Arsenal, but the comments do suggest they are looking to improve their position in the squad.

He also underlined the importance of having good cover, with Spain boss Luis de la Fuente believing players coming off the bench can be just as vital as those starting.

This is something Arsenal will want their squad to take on board. They will not always be able to play the same midfielders due to the demands of playing in both domestic and European competitions.

There is still time for Merino and Zubimendi to turn their situation around, so what they are doing now may not indicate how important they are going to be in the campaign.

Arsenal will be keen to keep Merino happy, and he has made his position clear. This should give some reassurance ahead of the January transfer window.

#1958. Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal show their resilience with impressive draw against Barcelona

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal Women claimed a vital point at the Camp Nou. They drew 1-1 against Barcelona in the Champions League on Thursday night.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in the first half. Caroline Graham Hansen scored to bring the game level after the break. Whilst Renee Slegers will be disappointed to miss out on all three points, her side played some encouraging football.

Despite needing to play differently, Arsenal had an even game against an opposition who would inevitably have long periods of the ball. The visitors played very well defensively and looked dangerous when they could attack.

The result showed that Slegers has a team that can adapt to new challenges. This could be important for Arsenal as they try to make a mark in Europe.

One of the key decisions made by Slegers was to include Maanum. She had only recently returned from injury but made an impressive impact against Barcelona.

The midfielder scored early on to start the game in the right direction. Slegers was very impressed with her play when not in possession. She was praised for her communication skills and assisting others.

Arsenal’s attacking play was mainly based on fast counter attacks. They knew they wouldn’t be able to play in the same style as Barcelona and therefore tried to take advantage of the space on offer.

However, there were chances created in both halves. Arsenal may have been more clinical with their chances, they were always a threat.

Eventually, Barcelona scored their equaliser through Graham Hansen. Slegers said that Arsenal lost their shape during the move, which gave Hansen too much space.

It was a reminder of how quickly Barcelona can strike if you lose your concentration for a moment.

The Arsenal manager was pleased with the way her players implemented the game plan, showing tenacity, discipline, good communication and bravery.

Slegers admitted Arsenal did lose the ball too much in the second half, and by keeping it longer, they would have taken the pressure off defending against Barca’s dangerous attack.

There was some frustration that Arsenal couldn’t hold onto their lead, and there were more chances created towards the end of the game. The visitors got into good positions to win corners but couldn’t get the winning goal.

They will feel very positive from their display. They put themselves up against one of the biggest tests in the Camp Nou and proved that they can cause Barcelona problems.

There isn’t much time to really reflect on the result ahead of their game against the London City Lionesses on Sunday, but Slegers now has another example of what her side can do when they play with purpose and structure.

The FA Youth Cup third round has been drawn and the Newcastle United youth handed the toughest of ties against Manchester City.

To make things even harder, the Newcastle United Under 18s drawn away from home.

No confirmed date and time as yet but all FA Youth Cup third round ties need to be played by Saturday 12 December.

If scores are level after 90 minutes that will be followed by 30 minutes of extra time, then a penalty shoot-out if still level after that.

The Newcastle United Under 18s have been transformed after the change of club ownership five years ago.

Starved of proper investment for a decade and a half under Mike Ashley, the NUFC youth team were regular strugglers, finishing at the bottom end of their league season after season.

Now with proper investment in recruitment, coaches and facilities under the current Newcastle United owners, the Newcastle United Under 18s are competing at the top end.

Last season they finished below only Manchester City and Manchester United in the Under 18s league (North) and this 2026-27 season it is the same three in the same order at the top end of the table.

The Manchester City Under 18s have won all eight league matches this season and scored 33 goals, plus they are aiming to win their third FA Youth Cup title in four seasons.

It will be a massive achievement if the Newcastle United Under 18s can go away and win this FA Youth Cup third round tie.

#1956. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

The draw is expected to get underway at 5pm.

#1955. West Ham Face Solomon Fitness Scare Ahead Of Preston

West Ham United winger Manor Solomon is struggling with back pain while on international duty with Israel, raising fresh concerns about his fitness ahead of the Hammers’ Championship clash with Preston North End.

According to Israeli publication Walla Sport, Solomon was only able to complete part of Wednesday’s training session ahead of Saturday’s Nations League match against Kosovo. The winger participated in the opening stages before withdrawing from the remainder of the session.

A further report on Thursday morning suggested that Solomon remained a doubt for the fixture, with his fitness due to be assessed again. There has been no confirmed withdrawal from the Israel squad, but given his recent problems, this is hardly the news West Ham supporters will have wanted to hear.

I am fully aware I might be contradicting myself here, having previously wanted Solomon to play for his country as a way of kick-starting his West Ham form. But this injury concern does cast the situation in a completely new light.

I understand that the left winger is an important player for Israel, but as I’ve made the case repeatedly, I believe his poor form is a direct result of him being overplayed by his country during the last international break.

Indeed, Claret & Hugh reported Solomon’s back problems during the October international break, when a club source confirmed that the winger was suffering considerable pain.

And if he is injured, or even feeling some pain in training, there is no way he should be risked against Kosovo.

There is simply too much at stake for West Ham to have a player returning from international duty in a worse physical condition than when he left.

That said, I do think Edvin Austbø has moved ahead of Solomon in the pecking order to start against Preston on West Ham’s left wing.

Solomon has struggled to find his best form, while Austbø has been pushing hard for an opportunity to impress new gaffer Scott Parker. Even if both players return fully fit, I would be inclined to give the Norwegian the starting place.

But with the competition in the EFL Championship starting to get very serious, I do hope that West Ham officials will be on to the Israel national team, pleading with them not to play Solomon unless he is 100% fully fit.

There is no suggestion at this stage that Solomon will miss the Preston match, and hopefully this turns out to be nothing more than a precaution.

However, given what happened during the previous international break, surely the sensible thing is to avoid taking any unnecessary risks.

#1953. Alan Shearer explains why Ezri Konsa has impressed him

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Alan Shearer believes Ezri Konsa has been the Premier League’s best player this season after an impressive start to his Arsenal career.

But the former Newcastle United striker has been impressed by the Gunners’ backline and feels Konsa should take a large amount of credit for the fact that they have not missed William Saliba so much.

Konsa’s arrival at Emirates has provided Mikel Arteta with a defender, but his performances have caused some issues for the Arsenal boss. Konsa is now a viable option for Arteta to play, as Saliba is fit again.

Shearer feels Konsa has done enough to be regarded as the best player in the division so far.

He stated in the Metro that Konsa has been effective while playing for Arsenal in the defence.

The former Newcastle player believed that Konsa has been the best player in the Premier League during this season. He pointed out the proof of the performance in the defence, arguing that people did not notice the missing Saliba until now.

Konsa has proved just how much he has grown since moving to the Emirates. Arsenal have been very strong at the back with Konsa playing a massive part.

But there is a problem with Konsa’s performances. Even if Saliba is fit he has done more than enough to make his place difficult to take.

Saliba is still one of Arsenal’s most important defenders, so Arteta will be delighted to have him back. However, he can’t ignore what Konsa has done in his absence.

It would be a tough call to leave the Englishman out, as he has been in such great form. But it means an experienced first choice defender would be left on the bench.

Konsa and Saliba could make a good partnership if they are given time to understand each other on the pitch. They will need to play regularly to do this.

#1951. Scott Parker Has Two Weeks To Solve West Ham’s Pressing Problem

West Ham have been given a fairly clear indication of what to expect from Preston North End when the two sides meet after the international break. Preston manager Graham Alexander has been explaining the aggressive pressing approach that helped his team beat Southampton, and it’s something Scott Parker will undoubtedly need to consider.

Speaking to the Lancashire Evening Post following the victory, Alexander said: “We pressed everything.” Preston outshot Southampton 12-3 in the first half, and their manager intends to use the break to reinforce that approach.

Without wishing to belittle Preston’s performance against Southampton, I have to say West Ham are in big trouble if we can’t beat them, irrespective of what their press might be. We can analyse the opposition’s tactics until we’re blue in the face, but ultimately West Ham should have enough quality to overcome Preston.

Parker has two weeks on the training ground to drill his players, and I would expect that time to be significant. He’s barely had an opportunity to work properly with the squad since replacing Nuno Espírito Santo, something that was evident during the defeat at Blackburn Rovers.

Parker has a philosophy of wanting to keep the ball, so I suspect he’ll want West Ham to play their way through Preston’s press rather than simply bypassing it with long balls. Of course, that requires players who are comfortable receiving possession under pressure and know where their next pass is going.

I also believe we’ll see a specialist defensive midfielder, such as Soungoutou Magassa, used more often than not for the remainder of the season. Parker has already shown a willingness to use Magassa, and having somebody in that position could prove particularly important when opponents attempt to press West Ham high up the pitch.

Preston’s victory over Southampton was a decent result, but it doesn’t suddenly make them an opponent West Ham should fear. Quite frankly, if the Hammers can’t beat the likes of Preston in our own backyard we don’t deserve to get promoted.

Parker has been given a valuable fortnight to work on his methods, and the expectation has to be that we return from the international break looking considerably better organised.

Whether Preston press high, sit deep or alternate between the two, West Ham need to be capable of dealing with it. That’s the challenge facing Parker, and I don’t think it’s an unreasonable expectation.
