The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1932. West Ham-Linked Rangers Giant Features In Spain Victory

West Ham United transfer target Ryan Naderi was handed a starting place for Czechia against Spain in Thursday night’s UEFA Nations League encounter, which ended in a 2-0 victory for the Spanish.

The 6ft 4in Rangers striker, who has recently been linked with a January move to West Ham, played 66 minutes before being substituted. Spain took the lead through an Álex Baena penalty in the 39th minute, with Marc Pubill adding a second deep into stoppage time.

There was another West Ham connection to the match, with Tomáš Souček returning to international action as an 85th-minute substitute as Marin covered earlier today. Former Hammers Vladimír Coufal and Alex Král were also in the Czech starting line-up.

As Claret & Hugh reported yesterday, West Ham have been linked with Naderi following his impressive start to life at Rangers.

The 23-year-old has reportedly attracted interest from several clubs, although Rangers are understood to be reluctant to sell their striker during the January transfer window. Spain’s victory leaves them with five wins from five Nations League fixtures.

That sets up a particularly interesting encounter with England at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on Sunday evening. The three lions spluttered to a 2-1 victory against Slaven Bilic’s Croatia last with Harry Kane scoring the winner from the spot.

The two sides are competing for top spot in Group A3, with the match kicking off at 7.45pm GMT.

Meanwhile, from a West Ham perspective, it is encouraging to see Souček back on the pitch following his recent injury problems, even if his involvement was limited to the closing stages.

#1931. GdS: Milan ready €50m January assault for Tresoldi to give Ramos a partner – the strategy

AC Milan are serious about signing Nicolo Tresoldi from Club Brugge, with an attempt being readied ahead of the winter window.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan intend to sign another striker even before the summer arrives, in order to boost their Champions League hopes. The name that they have chosen is someone the fans already know well: Nicolo Tresoldi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

At the end of June, the club announced the signing of Gonçalo Ramos for over €70m, the most expensive signing in the club’s history to date (and likely for a while to come). Ramos hasn’t – at least for now – cured Milan’s goal-scoring deficiency in the No.9 role.

The negotiations for Tresoldi, however, are shaping up to be costly. Last summer, Club Brugge rejected another Italian offer of €35m from Roma, and in the meantime the price has skyrocketed after the forward bagged 13 goals in 15 games.

Adding his four goals this season against Germany’s youth team brings him close to 20 for the season already. His league hat-trick against VV Sint-Truiden at the end of October followed his hat-trick at San Siro against Inter, marking the night that every Rossoneri fan knew his name.

Therefore, the cost could now be around €50m, another huge expense if Milan really decide to go all-in. The club made a €24m loss in the last accounts after three years of profit, and the temptation is to speculate to accumulate, i.e. to invest more and make sure of the Champions League revenues.

There’s a desire to finalise the deal as early as the January transfer window, unless Brugge move to raise the price, perhaps due to a potential foreign competition. Milan believe that their relationship with the Belgian side is actually strong, with Gerry Cardinale ready to lead talks again.

As for Ramos, the investment so far has yielded just three goals and two assists, which doesn’t mean he wasn’t effective and is ready to be shelved, but it’s precisely when paired with another striker that the management believes the Portuguese could be more productive.

In short, a two-striker team can’t be ruled out in the future, with Tresoldi alongside the former Benfica man. In the European race goals fuel the climb, and Milan know this after last season’s late collapse, keen to avoid it again.

Should Milan hit a wall erected by Club Brugge, they would leave the Tresoldi option open for the summer. In the meantime, they would fill the gap with a striker on loan from a top European club.

However, Tresoldi could provide an initial assist for Milan: his support for the Rossoneri is well-known and has been publicly stated, so among the various options available, Nicolò would choose the San Siro.

A permanent return to Italy could also benefit coach Roberto Mancini, who – after the Under-21 European Championship (which Tresoldi will compete in with Germany) – would finally like him to play for the senior Azzurri side.

Nicolò, born in Cagliari in August 2004, is still free to choose which (senior) national team he wants to represent, and Mancini expressed his confidence earlier this week: “I spoke to Tresoldi, and Ranieri spoke to us too. First of all, I think he needs to feel the desire to play for Italy.

“He was born in Italy, like his father [former defender Emanuele], who played for the Under-21s and won the European Championship. I think there’s a chance he’ll choose the Azzurri. He knows he can be an important player for our future, and I hope he makes the right choice.”

#1930. Shrewd appointments usher in new era of reconciliation | West Ham News

Very slowly, with each new hire, be it high profile such as a head coach, or a less visible appointment behind the scenes, West Ham United is travelling in a new direction. The combative era of Sullivan and Brady calling supporters their ‘customers’ and riding roughshod over fan opinions seems well and truly in the past.

Their new hire – head of supporter services and fan engagement (she’ll never get that job title on a business card) Arsenal’s Khali Parsons is a sign of the direction of travel as the Club attempts to heal ten years plus of division between owners and supporters that has been a corrosive backdrop to the football club’s history since before the move from Upton Park.

Nothing, of course, can change the hugely unpopular sale of the old ground and the dissatisfaction over the ‘rented home’ which the club now occupy, but there does appear to have been some serious ‘listening’ going on rather than the scant lip service paid to supporters’ grievances by Karren Brady in the bad old days.

According to westhamworld.co.uk“Parsons will officially take up the role in January 2027 and will also become the club co-chair of West Ham’s Fan Advisory Board, replacing Paul Stringer, [Chief Marketing and Media officer] who is filling the position on an interim basis….Her arrival comes at an important time for West Ham, with the club’s senior leadership structure changing significantly and supporter trust one of the issues the new hierarchy has openly acknowledged needs rebuilding.”

Cult Hero Martin in his playing days at West Ham – now goal keeping coach for u21’s

Indeed, the news also that former Hammer David Martin is to return to the club as u21 goal keeping coach could be seen as further news of a return to a club better in touch with, and more comfortable with it’s own heritage.

Not quite sure how it will feel as a West Ham fan, all of this unity after so many years of protest. Heaven help us if we also start winning games again: We really will have to pinch ourselves.

#1929. ‘If I stayed…’ – Rio Ngumoha reflects on ‘no-brainer’ decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool

Rio Ngumoha has said that his decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool in 2024 was a ‘no-brainer’.

The Reds signed the teenage winger from the London club’s academy just after he turned 16, with a subsequent tribunal determining that the Merseysiders were to pay an initial £2.8m (potentially rising to £6.8m) in compensation.

The now 18-year-old has gone on to make 44 appearances and counting for LFC’s first team, along with winning three senior England caps, and he’s turned in some man-of-the-match performances at Champions League level.

In a recent media interview (via The Standard), Ngumoha explained that he decided to leave Chelsea for Liverpool because he saw a clearer pathway to the first team at Anfield than he did in west London.

The winger said: “I needed a new challenge. I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea… not saying I wouldn’t have got to the first team as quickly, because I believe in my ability, but I feel Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

“The plan they set for me was straightforward. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Reds have had a fine track record for attracting top-class teenage talents in recent years, and Ngumoha is perhaps the standout signing in that category.

That Liverpool were prepared to go through a rigorous registration process with the Premier League (as the winger was a minor at the time) shows just how determined they were to see the deal through, and all of that bureaucratic effort has proven to be more than worth it.

In little more than a year, the teenager has gone from highly-rated prospect to established first-team presence, and there’s a palpable excitement among the fans at Anfield every time he gets the ball, with many a defender bamboozled by his phenomenal dribbling ability and supreme self-confidence.

Ngumoha’s leap of faith in joining the Reds has been vindicated by his regularity of senior football, especially this season as he’s started almost half of our matches across all competitions, and full credit to him for seizing his opportunity when it’s been handed to him.

Chelsea’s loss has very much proven to be our gain, and with the 18-year-old now holding a market value of €50m (£41.8m), that aforementioned compensation fee looks increasingly like one of the steals of the century.

#1928. West Ham Ticket Row: A Bit Of Pettiness? I’m All For It

West Ham United’s ticketing arrangements for the forthcoming Championship clash with Bristol City have caused controversy, but I have to say I’m firmly on the Hammers’ side with this one. If there’s an element of tit for tat involved, I don’t have a problem with it at all.

Bristol City supporters might not particularly like the situation, but there is some history between the two clubs when it comes to ticket allocations. During the FA Cup meeting in January 2024, Bristol City took their full allocation of around 9,000 tickets at the London Stadium, resulting in thousands of West Ham season-ticket holders having to move from their usual seats.

That caused considerable frustration at the time, with the West Ham United Supporters’ Trust seeking clarification from the club over the arrangements. So if the current situation feels like a bit of payback, I can certainly understand why.

One thing West Ham’s relegation to the Championship has provided is a real reality check when it comes to the treatment of travelling supporters.

In the Premier League, there was at least some collective understanding that away supporters shouldn’t be completely fleeced. The Football Supporters’ Federation’s original Twenty’s Plenty campaign eventually helped bring about the £30 away-ticket cap, which has remained in place since 2016.

It wasn’t perfect, and £30 was still more than supporters had originally campaigned for, but at least there was a limit.

That protection doesn’t exist across the Championship, and we’re now seeing the difference.

Take West Ham’s trip to Birmingham City in December, for example. According to the club’s official ticket information, adult supporters will be charged £37.50 for the privilege of watching the Hammers at St Andrew’s.

And it definitely feels like Championship clubs are treating us like absolute mugs.

When West Ham roll into town, we’re seen as a cash cow. Clubs know we’re going to bring a substantial travelling support, and it increasingly feels as though they’re happy to make the most of it.

Of course, I understand that Championship clubs have their own financial pressures, but that doesn’t make it any easier for supporters who are already spending a fortune travelling around the country.

I don’t have a problem with West Ham looking after our own fans, even if that means upsetting a few visiting supporters along the way.

Perhaps there’s a little bit of pettiness involved, but realistically, I don’t mind that either.

We’re West Ham, and the club should be looking after our fans. That ought to be the priority, particularly when supporters have been asked to put up with so much since dropping into the Championship.

And any Bristol City fans who don’t like it probably should look at their own club’s conduct when we played them in the FA Cup.

I don’t particularly want to see football clubs getting into an endless argument over ticket allocations, and ultimately I’d prefer supporters everywhere to be treated fairly.

But when it comes to this particular situation, I’m not going to criticise the West Ham hierarchy for giving a bit back.

Sometimes tit for tat is exactly what it looks like, and on this occasion, I’m perfectly happy with it.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

The tit-for-tat refers to Bristol City only receiving 2110 tickets for their visit to London Stadium, with the suggestion being that this was done due to Bristol City nit giving West Ham the 3,400 allocation that some teams receive.

This could all leave commentators with egg on their face if it turns out that this was the number of tickets that Bristol City requested.

#1926. MN: Why Milan and Inter are calm despite Council request over new stadium plan

A potential obstacle has already arisen after the Generali Stadium announcement, even if all parties remain calm for now.

As MilanNews recall, Tuesday morning’s edition of Corriere della Sera carried a report that had everyone on edge, just days after the renderings of the project were published. However, by the afternoon some quite important clarifications had arrived from Mayor Giuseppe Sala.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The newspaper reported that the Milan City Council had approved a bipartisan measure to halt the current environmental assessment process for the Generali Stadium project and request a new one that encompasses all the interventions the two clubs intend to undertake.

This includes the demolition of the current stadium once the new stadium is operational. The goal is to make the green light for the work conditional on a prior Health Impact Assessment (HIA).

MilanNews have learned that the City Council’s motion is non-binding, meaning Mayor Sala’s administration will not be obligated to follow the council’s request. More importantly, it does not suspend the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA).

The two clubs remain calm regarding the next phases, especially since the SEA and the VIS are two separate and distinct phases that must both be addressed before work on the new stadium can begin.

The Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a procedure established by Italian and European legislation that evaluates the environmental sustainability of a plan or program prior to its approval.

It differs from the subsequent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), which instead examines the environmental effects of a specific project prior to its potential authorisation and implementation.

The Council has therefore advanced a request that would not currently be foreseen under normal formal procedures. In any case, the two clubs are confident in the material produced, providing even more than necessary by integrating the Environmental Report with all the health-related details currently available.

Milan and Inter have no intention of avoiding any type of assessment. On the contrary, the EIA is scheduled for early 2027, by spring, with completion expected within a few months. Further investigations into the project and its impacts will therefore be undertaken shortly, as per the timetable.

Yesterday afternoon, Mayor Sala issues a statement on the news that broke, once again emphasising that the project will move forward.

“It’s clear that continuing to call the stadium issue into question is a gift to the right. I don’t want us to delude ourselves into thinking we’ve already won. I respect the City Council’s opinion, but the Council will respect the fact that I have no intention of reconsidering,” he said.

“We’ll discuss it in the City Council, but I have no intention of reconsidering the stadium. We’ve been talking about it for three years; everyone should do what they think best. I will continue to be consistent, and I will try to move forward with the stadium project.”

Councillor Martina Riva also gave a comment to MilanNews too: “Small obstacles? They won’t be a problem, we are convinced of the validity of our operation and we will move forward: the city, the teams and the fans who want a fully accessible stadium deserve it.

“I really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectationsaccessibleI really like the Generali Stadium, it has exceeded all expectations.”

#1924. ‘Unlikely to be…’ – Journalist sounds contract renewal warning over Van Dijk and Alisson

Liverpool fans have been advised that prospective contract renewals for Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker could take time to materialise.

The future of both long-serving players has been in the spotlight this week after they publicly addressed their respective situations, with the goalkeeper’s agent already in talks with club chiefs while the captain has maintained a more neutral ‘let’s see’ stance.

Their current deals are set to expire next June, and they’ll be able to sign pre-contract agreements with overseas clubs from the beginning of January unless they extend their terms with the Reds before then.

In an article for The Athletic discussing the futures of Van Dijk and Alisson, James Pearce warned that ‘there is unlikely to be a quick resolution’ to either player’s contract situation, citing how renewals for the Dutchman and Mo Salah two seasons ago weren’t confirmed until April 2025.

The journalist explained how Liverpool would need to take a pragmatic approach to the renewal process and not be led by sentiment, with the defender turning 36 next July and the goalkeeper’s 35th birthday coming three months later.

In a more hopeful note, Pearce wrote: ‘It makes sense for all parties to wait and see how things unfold in the coming weeks and months. Respect abounds and relationships are strong, with dialogue ongoing between sporting director Julian Ward and the pair’s camps.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The case studies of Van Dijk and Salah from 2024/25 indicate that we ought not to expect a swift resolution to the current contract situations regarding the Dutchman and Alisson, with negotiations set to involve substantial back-and-forth before any agreement is struck.

Considering ther importance on the pitch, they’re two of the highest-earning players in the current Liverpool squad, with the captain leading the way on £350,000 per week and the goalkeeper pocketing a weekly wage of £250,000 (Capology).

For their deals to be renewed, it’d either take a significant deflection from club policy to hand out lucrative extensions to players in their mid-30s, or the pair to accept a reduction on their base salary and increase the value of performance-related bonuses on offer.

In truth, the contract negotiations for Van Dijk and Alisson will likely run for another few months, and there could be some frayed nerves among Kopites if either or both situations were still unresolved by spring.

However, with the duo proving this season that they remain top-class performers bringing some crucial stability to a much-changed team, Ward must make every effort to keep them at Anfield for at least another year, and we’re cautiously optimistic that both will remain Reds players going into the 2027/28 campaign.

#1920. “Cashing in” on Castellanos claim ignores one major stumbling block | West Ham News

Ever since the closing days of the summer transfer window there have been claims that West Ham will be cashing in on Taty Castellanos in the winter: The Argentine has been a huge disappointment in the 15 games of West Ham’s championship season, with just a solitary goal to show for his efforts.

At times he’s resembled more of a moody, disinterested bystander and seems pretty much the most likely player in the eleven to be yellow carded each time he plays.

A solitary goal is plain unacceptable for the frontman who cost £27 million: Claims that he’ll be sold in the winter abound.

Sadly, Everton’s late interest in the summer window, reportedly around £40 million, appears to have evaporated as Taty’s form has waned. Understandably.

Far from happy: One goal in fifteen means Castellanos has been a huge let down in the second tier. Its also means those big money suitors have now evaporated

The newest suggestions from EFL specialist site the72.co.uk suggest Castellanos could be heading back home – however there’s a catch:

“River Plate reportedly view the 28-year-old as a priority target in their striker search, although the finances involved in the deal could prove to be a major hurdle. However, cashing in could give WHUFC the chance to sign a true talisman to aid their promotion bid. “

“Cashing in”? I think not: That’s the elephant in the room here. River Plate have already disclosed that they’ll look at some kind of loan or shared purchase option – as they’re short of funds – which of course will cut no ice with West Ham who will want to replace Taty with a striker more suited to scoring the Championship goals they require.

Merely shipping Taty out on loan without a permanent sale will serve no useful purpose and could actually weaken Scott Parker’s squad. The Hammers have enough loaned – out unwanted stars as it is: Another one added to the list won’t help a rebuild. The only possible route could involve a swap for goal keeper Santiago Beltran – which would still leave the Hammers short of a goal scorer and needing to offload Hermansen or Areola in the winter.

And how often to these player swaps ever come off? Exactly.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Fans of my vintage will probably remember we got Trevor sinclair on a swap deal from QPR for 2 of our players. I think tim breaker was one can’t remember the other what a deal that was.

Can’t blame Taty or Piroe really as neither have had a decent run of games and hardly no service at all.

#1919. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

"Incredible talent." 🌟Steven Gerrard reacts to Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola.🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/bVd7odopa3

"It was the shared vision." 🤝Oliver Glasner on why he chose to join the Nottingham Forest project 👀 pic.twitter.com/ldxjwU8FW4

"For me, it's a special game, definitely." ❤️Andoni Iraola looks ahead to his first Premier League game at Anfield as Liverpool boss.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fukilMigKz

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1918. “I don’t know why…” – John Aldridge fears Liverpool’s stance on one player could ‘backfire’

John Aldridge has questioned why Liverpool weren’t more assertive in pulling Dominik Szoboszlai out of national team duty when he’s currently nursing a minor injury.

The midfielder sprained his ankle in the 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola uncertain after the game as to whether or not the 26-year-old would join up with his country during this international window.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Hungarian FA said that a decision on the player’s participation against Georgia and Northern Ireland over the next week will be deferred until the ‘last minute’ as his fitness continues to be assessed.

In his latest column for the Liverpool Echo, Aldridge voiced his belief that Liverpool should’ve done more to prevent Szoboszlai from playing for Hungary in the coming days when he’s clearly not fully fit.

The former Reds striker wrote: ‘I know Virgil van Dijk has pulled out of the Netherlands squad because of a little niggle, but Dominik Szoboszlai has stayed with Hungary despite injuring his knee against Palace.

‘Any other club would pull them out of international duty. Manchester United, Arsenal, Man City – they’d all pull them. We’ve seen it before. Any doubt and that’s it, decision made, you’re not playing. I don’t understand why we don’t throw our weight around like that.

‘I understand players want to play for their country. I was the same with Ireland. I would answer call-ups even when I was injured. I get what it means and how much it means to players, but any other club would just pull them. That’s not happened here, I don’t know why. Hopefully that just means it’s not that serious.

‘It still sounds like they’re taking a risk. If he stays with Hungary and plays, we’ve just got to hope the decision doesn’t backfire and come back to hurt Liverpool.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

As Szoboszlai is contracted to Liverpool, the Merseyside club could’ve blocked him from representing his country during this international window because of his knee injury.

However, it’d appear to be a case of the player wanting to at least link up with the Hungary camp and try to prove his fitness, and Anfield chiefs green-lighting that action out of respect for the 26-year-old and not wanting to antagonise him by forbidding him to travel.

The grey area over the midfielder potentially being fit enough to play but not certain of doing so has presented a tricky dilemma, as much as Iraola would no doubt have preferred for our number 8 to swerve national team duty and prioritise his club instead.

With Hungary not playing until Saturday, that does give Szoboszlai a bit of time to recover from the knee issue he incurred at Selhurst Park, and we’d like to think that Marco Rossi wouldn’t risk fielding him against Georgia unless he’s definitely OK to feature.

While a swift return to action for the 26-year-old would obviously be a good thing, we just hope it doesn’t come at the expense of his involvement for Liverpool in the coming weeks, especially with a hectic run of 11 matches in 40 days before the end of December.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

It is all very well and good for pundits (code word for writers with preposterous assertions) to voice the opinion that LFC should have been more assertive in voicing their opinion on Szoboszlai not starting for Hungary. The problem with that line of thinking is that Szobo is always passionate to play for his country (and as seen last year in his performances to play for LFC), so if you deny him the right to play, you run the risk of alienating him, something Aldridge does not have to concern himself with because he has nothing to do with LFC or Szobo. I also worry that if he is allowed to start when not fit he will further injure himself, but believe Szobo and his manager will not take that action if he is not fit and can understand that Szobo as his country’s captain, if he does not start he would at least like to be on the sidelines giving his teammates moral support – something Aldridge also does not have to concern himself with! #1917. Scott Parker’s very own “Kevin Nolan” signing could be on the cards | West Ham News

Transfer stories have leapt with the arrival of new head coach Scott Parker – each manager has his own ideas on the ideal shape of his squad and Parker’s preferences will be very different to those of his predecessor. #1916. The one key question on which nearly all West Ham fans are in agreement

It is not often that West Ham fans appear unified over anything, after recent seasons of strife, division, disagreement and dispute with the Sullivan and Brady leadership, it feels as if ‘disharmony’ has been the default setting.

Not, it seems, about everything. There is one hot topic on which a huge majority of West Ham fans are in almost total agreement.

According to the NY Times’ fan survey, the biggest consensus was not for the approval of the new manager – although there is a pretty strong 77% majority of fans who responded who give the appointment of Scott Parker the thumbs up.

The biggest single factor on which most West Ham supporters agree is the choice of goalkeeper. According to the survey:

“Of the fans surveyed, an overwhelming 85.4 per cent believe Alphonse Areola should reclaim the No 1 jersey from Mads Hermansen.

Likeable yes, dependable no: 85% of West Ham fans want Hermansen out of the team

Interestingly, though, a sizeable 62 per cent of supporters believe the travelling contingent at Ewood Park were not right to boo Hermansen.”

Eighty five percent of fans have had enough of the Dane’s inept performances in between the sticks, with one fan driven to comment that West Ham’s goal would be better defended simply by hanging a green jersey on the cross bar rather than continuing to select the out of form Hermansen.

Of course the fly in the ointment is that Areola has been reported as ‘unfit’ – whether that means third choice Finlay Herrick comes into consideration – who can say- but it’d be a brave selection for Parker to leave his number one on the bench if Areola isn’t ready for the Preston North End fixture next weekend, however much it seems supporters want to see Hermansen out of the team.

#1915. GdS: Milan open to Camarda loan to aid development – move abroad also possible

AC Milan’s plan to strengthen the attack in January could have a knock-on impact on Francesco Camarda’s fate, a report claims.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport makes the bold claim that Milan are readying a winter attempt for Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge. His price tag is already €50m, but the idea is to invest in the young striker and potentially pair him with Goncalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tresoldi’s fate intersects with that of Camarda. The Milan academy graduate has barely exceeded 100 minutes of playing time this season, 119 to be precise: 83 in the Europa League, with a single start against Salzburg, and another 36 in Serie A.

He hasn’t scored and had only one real chance to score, against Bologna. He needs to play to showcase his qualities, so the club believe it’s best to try do this elsewhere, before returning fit and ready to play for the Rossoneri.

The new development is that Camarda could develop at another Serie A team, or potentially return further enriched by experience abroad. There’s no shortage of options outside of Italy, but it will be a dry loan with no option to make it permanent.

Having arrived as a child in the Milan youth academy, he won an U15 Scudetto. He also achieved a historic record: with a federal exemption required because he was still a teenager, Camarda made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on 25 November 2023, late in the match against Fiorentina.

On that occasion, he became the youngest debutant in Serie A history (15 years, 8 months, and 15 days) and the youngest debutant in Milan’s history, surpassing the previous record set by Paolo Maldini, who made his debut at 16 years, 6 months, and 25 days.

In 2024, he signed his first professional contract and began his experience with Milan Futuro, the club’s second team, created specifically to nurture Milan’s talents, without necessarily having the need to send them elsewhere to develop.

That same season, at 16 years and 226 days, he became the youngest Italian player ever to make his Champions League debut. In 2025-26, it was time to try Serie A, where he could consistently play: he moved to Lecce, where, in 23 appearances, he scored his first (and so far only) league goal.

He was bought by the Giallorossi, and then bought back by Milan (who reserved a buy-back clause), with a contract extended until the summer of 2031 in the summer, plus an option for another year.

After progressing through Italy’s youth teams, Camarda truly found his calling with the U21s, scoring four goals in six games. He was also called up to the senior national team, playing for Baldini’s ‘experimental’ squad, making two appearances.

#1913. Left out: High mileage Hammer’s injury sparks longer term fitness worries | West Ham News

There’ll be some relief amongst the West Ham medical staff at Rush Green tonight knowing that Manor Solomon was left out of Israel’s match altogether after the winger could not train owing to the pain of an ongoing injury.

However there will be concern that this same issue which dogged Solomon through September might yet prevent him playing his full part in the busy run up to Christmas  – with its demanding schedule of nine games in a little over a month.

Solomon came back from the last international break in September looking washed out, and in truth, his performances since have been a disappointment after his early season impact and man-of-the-match award.

Solomon – early season form has fallen away as his back injury has made itself known

#1912. Premier League KMI panel issues emphatic verdict on Alexander Isak penalty decision v Arsenal

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has concluded that Liverpool should’ve had a penalty awarded for an offence by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak in their defeat to Arsenal earlier this month.

Five minutes after Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game at Anfield, the Swedish striker had his shirt pulled in the box by the Gunners defender, but neither on-field referee Andy Madley nor Stuart Attwell on VAR felt compelled to award a spot kick despite the transgression being clear.

The Reds’ head coach Andoni Iraola went as far as claiming that a penalty would’ve been awarded had our number 9 gone to ground instead of staying on his feet when his jersey was grabbed.

On Wednesday, the Premier League published the findings of several incidents reviewed by the KMI Panel, including the one involving Isak and Timber on 1 November.

Their verdict reads (via premierleague.com): ‘The panel felt that a penalty should have been awarded for a holding action by Timber on Isak, 4:1. One panellist considered the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress.

‘The majority also felt that VAR should have intervened to recommend an on-field review, 3:2, on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error. Two panellists considered that the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention.’

The KMI Panel concluded: ‘In this instance the panel deemed that Timber’s challenge on Isak met the threshold for a holding offence and should have resulted in a penalty kick, both on-field and through VAR intervention.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

How nice of the KMI Panel to come back and tell us what was so damn obvious at the time of the incident – or at least obvious to anyone not named Andy Madley or Stuart Attwell, or whichever member of the panel felt that the right decision was made on the day.

How that individual concluded that Timber’s actions lacked ‘clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress’ is baffling – the Liverpool striker would surely have gotten on the end of Bradley Barcola’s cross had his shirt not been so blatantly pulled.

The panel’s verdict today won’t come as much consolation to anyone involved with the Reds, who were deprived of a legitimate penalty which – if converted – could’ve significantly altered the course of a match that they lost 1-0.

It’s not much good being told in retrospect that the officials got it wrong; these are clear decisions that professional referees should be capable of getting correct at the time, especially when they have the fallback option of VAR.

We get that many incidents are subjective and that consensus will never be achieved when it comes to refereeing in the Premier League, but there’s simply no excuse for botching calls like the Timber/Isak incident 10 days ago.

AC Milan board member Riccardo Stefanelli has revealed the positive impressions he has received from Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim.

Milan have had a mixed start to the season on the field. They have won seven of their first 11 games in Serie A which is a decent return, and puts them in the top four. However, they have lost three of four in the Europa League, leaving them outside the top 24 spots.

Off the field, things continue to be very busy. Markus Krösche is all set to become the new Head of Football, which the new stadium project was launched late last month, and a bumper deal with Adidas has apparently been signed off on as well.

“I’m honoured. It’s an award that has acquired a very valid meaning over time, I’m happy about it. It was born from a contact with Gerry Cardinale. We met in July 2022 and began discussing football, fantasising about his ideas for the project.

“I remember that conflicting visions arose on how to do football and business, but today the approach taken is the one Cardinale personally wanted, with enthusiasm, confidence, and consistency. I’ve always been a Milan fan, and I couldn’t help but accept Gerry’s proposal.”

“Gerry has a great energy to do well. Milan must achieve sporting goals first, then there are external projects like the stadium, which are very important.

“I haven’t met him, but he’s a serious, young guy. The players love him. As a fan, you always want to be first, but this is a tough league with so many big teams. I’m pleased because you can see a project emerging.”

The new stadium is another crucial thing for the owner…
